prompt:
## Task
Do A and B name the same business concept (the same real-world thing, so the classes model one concept under different names)? Concepts that merely share attributes such as an id or a date are not the same.

### A
concept: Treatment Product
where: TreatmentService (uses), src/business/treatmentService.ts, component business
code:
=====SOURCE-BEGIN
return this.products.create({ name: productName, withdrawalDays });
=====SOURCE-END=====

### B

=====SOURCE-END=====

response.rationale: These are two different concepts. A is a treatment product: a catalog item with a name and withdrawal days, created through TreatmentProductRepository.create in src/business/treatmentService.ts ("return this.products.create({ name: productName, withdrawalDays });"). B is a treatment: a record of a treatment applied to a hive, stored as TreatmentRecord items in TreatmentRepository in src/persistence/repositories.ts ("private readonly items: TreatmentRecord[] = [];"). The graph backs this up. TreatmentService (node 2912145e8ad12343) calls two separate repositories: TreatmentProductRepository (create/findAll/findById/findByName) and TreatmentRepository (create/findByHive). TreatmentRepository (node b2566037ba6b6900) is looked up by hive. So a product is something used in a treatment, and a treatment is the event of applying it to a hive. They are related but not the same thing.
